The offer-level formulas combine an offer-level promotional connection with an existential gift component. For mixed offers, the same non-discount gift component must bear the required promotional connection; otherwise unrelated components could jointly produce an unsupported prohibition.

The source defines distributors in the context of distributing SFC-authorised funds. Broader distributor interpretations in node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249, node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b require reconciliation with that source scope. Conversely, node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f narrows the specific promoted product to an SFC-authorised fund although paragraph 10 says 'specific investment product'. Whether this reflects the circular's application or excludes covered cases remains unresolved.

The full Code of Conduct paragraph 3.11 and the answer to question 1 of the SFC FAQs issued on 30 September 2010, referenced in footnote 3, are missing. Their qualifications remain unchecked; the circular still directly supports the quoted gift rule. No external dependency IDs are supplied.

Guaranteed returns and incentives may be gifts; their status is not automatic. Fund return and distributor top-up must remain distinguishable when classifying components. A discount elsewhere in an offer cannot exempt a distinct non-discount gift.

Neither a discount exception nor TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT establishes compliance beyond the selected gift control. Section 103 authorisation is not a gift-rule exception, and structured-product status is not a prerequisite for the gift restriction.
